turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on a and an?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: use an before a word that starts with a vowel sound (an egg, an hour), and a before others.
Right: "An owl sleeps all day." Wrong: "A owl sleeps all day." The word owl starts with a vowel sound, so it needs an, not a.
Let me think aloud with one example: "The zoo has a camel." I look at the next word, camel. It starts with a c sound, not a vowel sound. So I choose a.
Now you try. Write a or an:
She has ___ orange in her bag. (answer with only the missing word)
